title: The Weekend With Lava La Rue

paragraphs.text: Date：17 July 2026
Tags：The Weekend With... Features
paragraphs.translation: 標籤：與...共度週末、專題報導

paragraphs.text: As Lava La Rue celebrates the release of their latest single Prince of Bologna, we go behind the scenes on what’s fuelling the multi-hyphenate’s creative output – from arthouse horror films to hardcore punk festivals.
paragraphs.translation: 隨著 Lava La Rue 慶祝他們最新單曲《Prince of Bologna》的發行，我們深入了解這位於斜槓創意人背後的創作動力——從藝術恐怖片到硬核龐克音樂節。

paragraphs.text: Genre-bending artist, musician and creative director of DIY arts and music collective NiNE8, Ava Laurel, AKA Lava La Rue, released a follow-up to their 2024 full-length studio debut Starface earlier this year in the form of a fresh EP: Do You Know Everything?, marking a shift in their sound with a full-band setup. Originating as a jam session amongst friends, the new set of tracks blends punk catharsis with indie-rock influences and was produced with the help of Grammy-winning producer Fraser T. Smith. That’s not all Lava had in store for this season though. The artist’s brand new single comes out today: Prince of Bologna – a song produced and released by Dan Carey’s (Fontaines D.C, Kneecap) indie label Speedy Wunderground. (Get listening: here)
paragraphs.translation: 橫跨多種流派的藝術家、音樂家，同時也是 DIY 藝術與音樂團體 NiNE8 的創意總監 Ava Laurel（藝名 Lava La Rue），在今年早些時候繼 2024 年首張全長錄音室專輯《Starface》後，推出了全新 EP《Do You Know Everything?》，標誌著他們轉向全樂隊編制的音色。這組新曲目最初源自朋友間的即興演奏，融合了龐克的宣洩感與獨立搖滾的影響，並在葛萊美獎製作人 Fraser T. Smith 的協助下完成。但這還不是 Lava 本季準備的所有內容。這位藝術家的全新單曲於今日發行：《Prince of Bologna》——這首歌是由 Dan Carey（曾合作過 Fontaines D.C, Kneecap）的獨立廠牌 Speedy Wunderground 製作並發行。（點此收聽）

paragraphs.text: To mark the release we caught up with the London-based musician about what’s feeding into their current creative inspirations behind the scenes. A perfect weekend with Lava looked a bit like this: family-run restaurant eats, left-field horror movies, hardcore punk festivals, a healthy dose of Greek mythology... oh and a BBQ on the beach!
paragraphs.translation: 為了紀念發行，我們與這位駐倫敦的音樂家聊了聊幕後激發他們目前創意靈感的事物。與 Lava 度過的完美週末大概是這樣的：家庭經營的餐廳美食、非主流恐怖片、硬核龐克音樂節、適量的希臘神話……喔，還有一場在海灘上的燒烤！

paragraphs.text: You’ll find me at...
paragraphs.translation: 你會在這些地方找到我...

paragraphs.text: “I’m definitely trying to finesse my way into Outbreak this year – Deftones, Amyl & The Sniffers, SALEM, IDLES, JPEGMAFIA & Show Me The Body all in one day at vicky park is insane! Hilarious that Esdeekid is on the bill too for what was known as a hardcore festival. I’m kinda here for it tho.”
paragraphs.translation: 「今年我絕對會想辦法潛入 Outbreak 音樂節——Deftones、Amyl & The Sniffers、SALEM、IDLES、JPEGMAFIA 和 Show Me The Body 同一天出現在維多利亞公園簡直瘋了！好笑的是 Esdeekid 竟然也在這個以硬核音樂節著稱的名單上。不過我倒挺支持的。」

paragraphs.text: “Someone left a copy of Maurice Cornforth’s Historical Materialism at the free library at Kensal Rise station and I honestly can’t put it down. It was released in the 50s but it’s still so relevant, a main point being that we spend all day arguing over what Marx calls ‘superstructure’ (politics, law, religion) but those things are a front, put in place to govern the ‘economic base’ which really rules the world (resources, technology, labour, ownership) and if we truly focused on that, we’d achieve progress much quicker.”
paragraphs.translation: 「有人在 Kensal Rise 車站的免費圖書館留了一本 Maurice Cornforth 的《歷史唯物主義》，我真的愛不釋手。這本書是在 50 年代出版的，但現在依然非常有意義，其核心觀點是我們整天在爭論馬克思所說的『上層建築』（政治、法律、宗教），但這些都只是表象，是為了管理真正統治世界的『經濟基礎』（資源、技術、勞動力、所有權）而設立的，如果我們能真正專注於此，我們就能更快取得進步。」

paragraphs.text: “Okasan Sushi is a cute little family-run Japanese restaurant in the heart of Portobello Market. Most people think going to a sushi restaurant is expensive but I go there to save money. I’ve watched the kids at that restaurant grow up and have ordered the same thing for seven years: teriyaki salmon with rice and a miso soup (with an Asahi if I’m in the mood). On a sunny day, sit outside and watch the people of Portobello.”
paragraphs.translation: 「Okasan Sushi 是一家位於波托貝洛市場中心、精緻可愛的家庭經營日式餐廳。大多數人認為去壽司店很貴，但我去那裡是為了省錢。我看著那家餐廳的孩子們長大，七年來都點同樣的東西：照燒鮭魚配飯和味噌湯（如果心情好的話再加一瓶朝日啤酒）。在陽光燦爛的日子裡，坐在外面觀察波托貝洛的人群。」

paragraphs.text: “Both my guitarist and partner are obsessed with horror movies. My guitarist frequents indie grindhouse cinema The Nickel in Farringdon, which exclusively plays vintage horror. I’ve been trying to get my tolerance up because they both love to pop a horror on in my living room. I’m curious to watch The Nickel’s screening of artistically influential The Holy Mountain (1973) to see what the hype’s about. It’s a good starting point for someone like me who prefers their horror ‘pretty to look at’… it’s giving avant-garde Midsommer vibes.”
paragraphs.translation: 「我的吉他手和伴侶都對恐怖片著迷。我的吉他手常去法靈頓的一家名為 The Nickel 的獨立磨坊電影院，那裡專門放映經典恐怖片。我一直在努力提高自己的耐受力，因為他們倆都喜歡在我客廳放恐怖片。我很想去看看 The Nickel 放映的極具藝術影響力的《聖山》（1973），看看它到底在紅什麼。對於像我這樣喜歡恐怖片要『好看』的人來說，這是一個很好的起點……它帶有一種前衛的《仲夏魘》氛圍。」

paragraphs.text: Something I’ve got my eye on…
paragraphs.translation: 我正關注的事物...

paragraphs.text: “There’s this nice dude Hammet in Bristol that makes custom guitars. He’s got one called the Nazaré that I would sell all my ribs to own but I don’t have any ribs left to sell… one day.”
paragraphs.translation: 「布里斯托有個叫 Hammet 的好人會做手工吉他。他有一款叫 Nazaré 的型號，我願意賣掉我所有的肋骨來擁有它，但我已經沒有肋骨可以賣了……總有一天會買到的。」

paragraphs.text: This is on repeat in my headphones…
paragraphs.translation: 我的耳機裡一直在重複播放...

paragraphs.text: “I’ve been listening to The Cramps a lot. But if I’m making music all day I need an ear rest and prefer to listen to three hours of Greek mythology to work or fall asleep to – sometimes they make it into my dreams, it’s pretty lit, I’ll be kicking it with Poseidon and shit. You gotta be careful though – a lot of long-form Greek mythology podcasts are AI-generated these days. I can only fall asleep to a real human voice.”
paragraphs.translation: 「我最近常聽 The Cramps。但如果我整天都在做音樂，我的耳朵需要休息，我喜歡在工作或入睡時聽三個小時的希臘神話——有時它們會進入我的夢境，這真的很酷，我會跟波賽頓之類的神混在一起。不過你得小心——現在很多長篇希臘神話播客都是 AI 生成的。我只能聽真人聲音入睡。」

paragraphs.text: A memento from your weekend with me...
paragraphs.translation: 與我共度週末的紀念品...

paragraphs.text: This is the space where creatives leave us with something to look at from the weekend we’ve spent with them. It could be anything really – a drawing, a picture or just something cool they think you should have a little look at.
paragraphs.translation: 這是創意人們在我們與他們共度週末後，留給我們觀賞的空間。它可以是任何東西——一幅畫、一張照片，或者只是他們認為你應該看一眼的酷東西。

paragraphs.text: “Londoners often forget Britain is a literal island… you’re always a simple train ride away from the coastline. Here’s me doing up a rocky beach Aldi BBQ lunch date on a perfect weekend. Deffo going in the memory scrapbook.”
paragraphs.translation: 「倫敦人常常忘記英國字面上就是個島嶼……你離海岸線永遠只有一趟火車的距離。這是我在一個完美的週末進行岩石海灘 Aldi 燒烤午餐約會的照片。絕對要收進回憶剪貼簿裡。」

paragraphs.text: Ellis Tree (she/her) is a staff writer at It’s Nice That. She joined as a junior writer in April 2024 after graduating from Kingston School of Art with a degree in Graphic Design. Across her research, writing and visual work she has a particular interest in printmaking, self-publishing and expanded approaches to photography. ert@itsnicethat.com
paragraphs.translation: Ellis Tree（她/她）是 It’s Nice That 的特約撰稿人。她在 2024 年 4 月從金斯頓藝術學院獲得平面設計學位後，以初級撰稿人的身份加入。在她的研究、寫作和視覺作品中，她對版畫製作、獨立出版和攝影的擴展方法特別感興趣。ert@itsnicethat.com
